on 10 October, 2025  124  HIGH COURT OF JAMMU & KASHMIR AND LADAKH  AT JAMMU Case: WP(C) No. 2820/2025 Sikander Kumar ..... Petitioner(s)
 Through :- Ms. Rozina Afzal, Adv.
 vs Jammu Municipal Corporation and others .....

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JAMMU & KASHMIR AND LADAKH  AT JAMMU
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent(s)
Through :- Ms. Monika Kohli, Sr. AAG

CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE WASIM SADIQ NARGAL, JUDGE  ORDER 10.10.2025 1.

Ms. Rozina Afzal, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has been continuously carrying out the vending business since 1999 and possesses a valid registration and license for the said purpose.

She has also drawn the attention of this Court to the registration certificate issued by the Department of Health and Medical Education, Government of J&K and Food Safety and Standards Authority of India under FSS ACT, 2006.

entities.text: Department of Health and Medical Education
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: A perusal thereof reveals that the said certificate was issued on 10.12.2020 and is valid up to 09.12.2025.

It is specific case of the petitioner that since 1999, the petitioner has been earning his livelihood by selling the vegetables and fruits on the cart(Rehri) and some time on stall in the Vegetable Market near Maheshpura Chowk, Bakshi Nagar, Jammu.

2. Ms. Afzal has further submitted that it is not only the petitioner, who is running the business of sale of fruits and vegetables, but there are 110 more persons/venders who are earning their livelihood by selling vegetables and fruits in the said vegetable market behind the grills.

It is specific case of the petitioner that the petitioner possess a valid license and registration for vending business for selling fruits and vegetables but the respondents are not allowing the petitioner to carry on his business of fruits and vegetables in the vegetable market at Maheshpura, Bakshi Nagar behind the grills under the garb of the encroachment drive in the said area.
It is contended that the respondents are not allowing the petitioner to run his business which is violative of the Article 21 of the Constitution.

3. Ms. Afzal has further drawn the attention of this Court to the order passed by a coordinate Bench Sikander Kumar vs Jammu Municipal Corporation And Others on 10 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156535315/
1 of this Court in the similar facts and circumstances of the case, wherein, the respondents intended to throw the petitioners therein/venders out and this Court after feeling prima facie satisfied by virtue of order dated 24.11.2013 passed in OWP No. 1771/2013 has restrained the respondents from dispossessing or interfering in the business activities of the petitioners therein, which is still operating, as such she prays for a same relief in the instant case, as well.
4.

entities.text: Sikander Kumar vs Jammu Municipal Corporation And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner at length.
5. Issue notice to the respondents, returnable within four weeks.
Notice in the CM as well.

Meanwhile, subject to objections and till next date before the Bench, the respondents are directed to allow the petitioner to continue his business of fruits and vegetables vending at Maheshpura Chowk, Bakshi Nagar, Jammu without any hindrance in light of the fact that the petitioner possess Registration Certificate for vending business issued by the Department of Health and Medical Education, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and the Municipality Corporation, Jammu,
dated 10.12.2020 and license bearing No. JMC/DC(N)/PSVL/2025-26/00023 issued by the Municipal Corporation, Jammu.
8. Modification/alteration on motion.
(WASIM SADIQ NARGAL) JUDGE JAMMU 10.10.2025
